findings.title: R2-05: zero-gated defect transfer between columns -1 and +1, and the log-rate it yields
findings.claim: With D_x(t) = a(t+P,x) XOR a(t,x): (1) D_{x-1}(t) = D_x(t+1) XOR [(a(t+P,x) OR a(t+P,x+1)) XOR (a(t,x) OR a(t,x+1))] for all t,x; (2) if D_0(t)=D_0(t+1)=0 then D_{-1}(t) = (1 XOR a(t,0)) AND D_{+1}(t); (3) a depth-2 analogue; (4) if the centre column is P-periodic from T then for every m >= T+P some s in [m-P, 2m-P] has D_{+1}(s)=1 with a(s,0)=0, so column +1 has at least log2(t)-O(1) period-P defects up to time t.
findings.scope: Rule 30, single black cell at the origin, new = left XOR (centre OR right). (1) is unconditional. (2),(3),(4) assume the negation of Problem 1 for column 0 with explicit transient T and period P. All four are proved by hand in REPORT.md; the finite checks run to t=1200 over ten periods.
findings.result: Hand proofs given. Finite verification passes every check: reconstruction identity 2,876,400 instances; defect recursion 317,682; locality 157,784 live defects; Prop 1 at 2,998 coincidental-hypothesis pairs; Prop 2 at 5,935 and 1,500; light-cone defect 11,534. The mask (1 XOR a(t,0)) is absent for rules 90 and 150, whose transfer is the unmasked XOR, verified separately.

verification.scope: rule 30 single seed, t <= 1200, periods {1,2,3,5,7,11,14,29,64,97}, columns -41..40; rule 90 contrast t < 300, columns -30..30. Python 3 stdlib, no Lean.

limitations: Theorem B bounds defects in column +1, not column 0; it is not by itself a step towards a contradiction.
Jen's theorem (already in the kit) gives infinitely many such defects without a rate; only the rate and the mask are new here.
log t is far below the positive density any charging route needs.
Prop 1, Prop 2 and Theorem B have hypotheses false for rule 30, so on the real orbit they are only checked where the hypothesis holds coincidentally.
findings.next_action: Prove a capacity lemma: one column +1 defect can terminate only O(1) of the light-cone sources (-m, m-P). That converts log t into positive density. Start by making the defect walk deterministic through the mask, which forces every column -1 site onto a zero of the centre.

findings.title: R2-05: rules 90 and 210 cap any shared-structure defect rate at O(log t), and the cap dies once the centre is known non-constant
findings.claim: Exactly four elementary rules are quiescent, black-left-edged and left-permutive: 30, 90, 150, 210. For rules 90 and 210 from the single black cell the centre column is white for all t >= 1 and column +1 is black exactly at t = 2^k - 1, so its period-1 defect count is 2*floor(log2(t+1)) + O(1). Hence no defect-rate lower bound better than O(log t) is provable from those three shared facts alone. Both witnesses have a WHITE centre; the kit already excludes an eventually constant column for rule 30, and the only remaining sibling, rule 150, has a constant BLACK centre with defect density 2/3. So under the non-constant hypothesis the family caps nothing.
findings.scope: All 256 elementary rules for the structural test; single black cell and t < 16384 for the three sibling orbits; period P = 1, transient T = 1.
findings.result: Family = {30,90,150,210} (exhaustive). Rules 90 and 210: column +1 black exactly at 2^k - 1 up to t = 16384; N_1(t)/log2(t) measured 1.81, 1.81, 1.96, 1.93 at t = 100, 1000, 10000, 16382; defect density 0.0016. Rule 150: centre constant black, defect density 0.6667. Theorem B's conclusion verified to hold on all three orbits.

verification.scope: 256-rule structural scan is exhaustive; orbit measurements are finite prefixes to t = 16384. The closed form t = 2^k - 1 is classical by Kummer's theorem but is not proved here.

limitations: The 2^k - 1 closed form is verified to t = 16384 and argued from Kummer, not formalized.
The cap says what shared hypotheses can prove, not that an argument using them must fail.

It applies to the coordinator's Golden defect clock only to the extent that clock's hypotheses are shared; its ether/No00/Golden restrictions are rule-30 specific, so this mirrors rather than explains that ceiling.
findings.next_action: Treat 'the hypothetical periodic centre is non-constant' as a usable hypothesis in any rate argument, since the kit already supplies it and it removes both log-rate witnesses.

findings.title: R2-05: 65,532 orbits of the shared-structure family realize period 1 and nothing else
findings.claim: Across rules {30,90,150,210} and every seed of width 1..14 with a black leftmost cell, no column is eventually periodic with a non-constant period. Rule 30 yields no eventually periodic column at all. The sibling-rule barrier to shared-structure arguments is therefore, on this evidence, a period-1 barrier only, and rule 30's period-1 case is already closed in the kit by a rule-30-specific monotonicity argument.
findings.scope: 65,532 orbits; columns -4..23 relative to the seed's leftmost cell (1,834,896 columns); t < 900; periods <= 32; transient <= 200; a period accepted only on a full suffix match.
findings.result: Eventually periodic columns found: rule 30 none; rule 90 494; rule 150 494; rule 210 15,639. Every one of them constant, minimal period 1. Zero non-constant eventually periodic columns in the whole family. The rule 30 result is the expected control: a period-2 hit there would contradict CQ01.

verification.scope: Stated box only. Bitwise evolver cross-checked against the independent bytearray evolver on all 28 columns to t = 300.

limitations: A finite box: widths <= 14, 28 columns near the seed, t < 900, periods <= 32, transients <= 200.
A long transient, a wider seed, a distant column or a period above 32 would be missed.
Shows only that the obvious refutation of a shared-structure argument for period >= 2 is absent, not that such an argument exists.
findings.next_action: Extend the box where it could change the answer: periods to 128 and transients to 2,000 on widths <= 10.

findings.title: R2-05: retraction of round-one F001 -- moving frame mistaken for fixed columns, and a missing left neighbour
findings.claim: Round one claimed that solving rule 30 for the right neighbour would widen a periodic strip rightwards, evidenced by a left side periodic to depth 160 against a right side with no period <= 400. The claim fails on three counts.
findings.scope: Retracts r30-coinailyzer-swarm-20261024T214719Z-1bf7da5f-v01#F001 in full. Recomputation on rule 30 single seed, t < 4000.
findings.result: (1) right = new XOR left requires column -1, whose periodicity the hypothesis does not supply and which Jen's theorem excludes once column 0 is assumed periodic. (2) The round-one probe tracked a window at fixed depth inside the light-cone edge, which moves one cell per step; at FIXED columns -160,-80,-20,-5,-1,0,1,5,20,80,160 no period <= 400 exists with transient <= 500, on the left exactly as on the right. The regular left region ends at depth 0.756-0.768 of t, i.e. x about -0.24t, matching the known rule 30 left-boundary speed near 0.25, so a fixed column leaves it forever after t = k/0.24. (3) The round-one probe searched periods up to 400 on a 400-sample window, so P = 400 passed on zero comparisons; with at least P real comparisons required, the right side reads 64 at depth 1 and no period at depths 5..160 instead of 64, 256, 256, none.

verification.scope: Rule 30 single seed, t < 4000; fixed-column periods <= 400 with transient <= 500; boundary by binary search on depth at t = 1000..3700.

limitations: Fixed-column aperiodicity is a bounded search and counts as falsification only, not a theorem.
The wedge boundary slope is an empirical estimate from six samples.
findings.next_action: Stop. The surviving content -- left-permutivity -- is prior art and is reused in F001 in the direction where it is deterministic.
